rounds.text: Cochin Minerals & Rutile Ltd trades at an attractive valuation with a price-to-earnings ratio of 8.34x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 4.93x that sits well below the sector benchmark of 10.49x [E11]. The financial health of the business is exceptionally strong, featuring zero debt at Rs 0 Cr as borrowings were completely wiped out from Rs 6 Cr a year earlier [E38], backed by robust cash generation where operating cash flow reached Rs 31 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs 25 Cr in Mar 2026 [E35, E36]. Fundamental momentum is accelerating sharply, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 46% [E17], a profit growth of 106% [E21], and a quarterly operating margin expansion of 8 percentage points in Sep 2026 compared to the year-ago period [E31]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model puts the intrinsic value at Rs 1242 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 70.5% [E43, E44], while the reverse DCF implies that the current market price incorrectly prices in a negative 3.0% earnings growth [E45]. Promoters have also demonstrated confidence by increasing their stake to 51.36% as of Sep 2026 [E40], operating within a chemical sector currently benefiting from a positive macroeconomic tailwind [E60]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 5 years is a sluggish 4% and 3-year sales growth contracted by 13% [E15, E16].

While recent trailing figures show sharp momentum, a deeper look reveals persistent structural growth problems, highlighted by a poor compounded sales growth of just 4% over the last five years and a concerning 13% decline over the past three years [E15, E16, E53]. Profitability trends reinforce this fragility, as 3-year compounded profit growth sits deeply in the red at -35% and the operating margin has compressed by 3 percentage points over the TTM period down to 10% [E16, E20, E30]. Furthermore, returns on equity remain underwhelming on a multi-year view, with a 3-year median ROE of 10%, a last-year median ROE of 9%, and an overall low 3-year average of 10.1% [E28, E29, E54]. Operational predictability is also questionable given that the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are both explicitly classified as inconsistent [E32, E33]. Compounding these concerns, institutional confidence is waning as domestic institutional holding has dropped to a negligible 0.07% from 0.62% [E41]. Conceded: the company carries zero debt, has generated strong operating and free cash flows of Rs 31 Cr and Rs 25 Cr respectively, and maintains a solid dividend payout of 49.9% [E35, E36, E38, E52].

Conceded: compounded 5-year sales growth is 4% and 3-year sales growth is -13% [E15, E16]. However, focusing entirely on those historical windows ignores a dramatic operational inflection; trailing twelve-month sales growth has surged by 46% [E17], with recent quarterly metrics demonstrating staggering year-over-year gains of 98% in sales and 333% in net profit [E56, E58]. Conceded: 3-year compounded profit growth is -35% and TTM operating margin compressed slightly to 10% [E20, E30]; nevertheless, the most recent quarterly operating margin recovered to 11%, representing an 8 percentage-point expansion over the year-ago quarter [E31]. Conceded: multi-year median ROE measures around 10% to 12% [E26, E28], yet the company's single-year ROCE sits at an elite 25.84% compared to a sector benchmark of just 11.11% [E10]. Conceded: operating margins are flagged as inconsistent [E32, E33] and domestic institutional holding has drifted down to 0.07% [E41], but these rearview-mirror concerns are entirely overshadowed by the fact that the company is completely debt-free with zero borrowings [E37, E38], backed by robust free cash flow of Rs 25 Cr [E36] and a healthy dividend payout of 49.9% [E52].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth surged by 46% and recent quarterly net profit rose 333% [E17, E58]. However, this explosive short-term rebound follows deep multi-year deterioration, including a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -13% and a 35% drop in compounded profit over the same window [E16, E20]. Conceded: single-year ROCE reaches 25.84% [E10] and the company is entirely debt-free [E37]; nevertheless, its fundamental profitability across broader time horizons remains subdued, marked by a 3-year median ROE of just 10% and a TTM ROE of only 9% [E28, E29]. Conceded: quarterly margins expanded by 8 percentage points year-over-year in September 2026 [E31]; yet the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are explicitly classified as inconsistent over the last two periods [E32, E33], reflecting ongoing cyclical volatility [E48]. Conceded: the company maintains robust free cash flow of Rs 25 Cr [E36]; however, domestic institutions have steadily abandoned the stock, cutting their holdings down to a negligible 0.07% [E41], while the rules-based screen scores a lukewarm 69 out of 100 with low confidence [E55].
